sentences.text: Nesotrochis was a genus of extinct flightless birds that lived exclusively on the islands of the Greater Antilles in the Caribbean.
Although often called cave rails, Nesotrochis is now classified as an independent lineage of gruiform birds rather than a true rail.
Three distinct species were identified: Nesotrochis debooyi from Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, Nesotrochis picapicensis from Cuba, and Nesotrochis steganinos from Hispaniola in Haiti.
These birds are considered examples of insular gigantism because their bodies were significantly larger than those of actual rails.
The group survived for an incredibly long time, ranging from 0.129 million years ago to the present.
Three species of Nesotrochis are known from subfossil remains discovered in cave deposits dating to the Late Pleistocene and Holocene.
A 2021 DNA analysis of the mitochondrial genome of N. steganinos confirmed that the genus is not a rail but an independent lineage of gruiform birds.
Research suggests the closest relatives of Nesotrochis are the African family Sarothruridae and the extinct New Zealand adzebills.
The parent group for the genus Nesotrochis is the family Nesotrochidae.
The type species of the genus Nesotrochis is Nesotrochis debooyi, the Antillean cave rail.
Nesotrochis fossils date from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene.
